items.title: 5 Stocks That Keep Raising Their Dividend Regardless Of The Market
items.summary: Some companies keep writing bigger dividend checks even when their end markets are shrinking, and the trait that separates them from the rest has nothing to do with yield. Five names across insurance, automation, and home improvement have quietly built that kind of durability.

items.title: Is LOW Stock A Buy As EPS Grows While Sales Shrink?
items.summary: Lowe's Companies (LOW) trades at $198, down about 26% over the past year while the S&P 500 (SPY) returned about 19%. The tape reads like a retailer stuck with a cautious DIY customer and a housing market management expects to recover only gradually. Its own numbers say something stranger: per-share earnings compounded higher over the past three years while revenue shrank.

items.title: Home Depot Drops 12.4% in a Month: Time to Buy or Stay Cautious?
items.summary: HD faces housing and cost pressures, but Pro momentum, digital growth and faster fulfillment support its long-term growth outlook.

items.title: AMD and Nvidia Just Experienced an Unprecedented Valuation Split
items.summary: Nvidia looks better on paper, yet trades at a cheaper valuation.

items.title: Stocks fall on Wall Street as oil prices jump back above $100 a barrel after Iran war escalates
items.summary: Stocks on Wall Street lost ground again Wednesday as the price of crude oil climbed back above $100 a barrel amid further escalation in the U.S. war with Iran.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.8%, and the Nasdaq composite gave up 0.6%.  Every sector within the benchmark S&P 500 declined except for energy, which rose as oil companies notched gains.

items.title: 1 Consumer Stock for Long-Term Investors and 2 Facing Challenges
items.summary: Retailers are adapting their business models as technology changes how people shop. But many seem to be moving too slowly as their demand is lagging, causing the industry to underperform the market - over the past six months, retail stocks’ 6.8% return has fallen short of the S&P 500’s 13.6% gain.

items.title: 3 Stocks Built for Higher Rates—And 2 That Could Break
items.summary: As Treasury yields near 4.79% amid rising rates, analysts argue the borrowing-cost-versus-return spread, not the headline rate, best explains winners like ASML and GE Vernova versus laggards like Oracle and Rocket.

items.title: Here's What to Expect Ahead of RH's Q2 Earnings Release
items.summary: RH's Q2 performance may reflect modest sales growth as housing weakness, sourcing disruptions and international startup costs weigh on results.
